text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and well grounded. Core numbers match the card: 45.6% of 241 claims, expected 8.2%, score 7.02, z 6.37, 13% low-complexity, 30 documented claims, 9 of 13 (69%) below billed, and 2 of 23 with no lab line. The 15% comparison rate matches the card's all_provider_rate of 0.147. The cited claims fit their sentences: C0049818, C0049848 and C0049952 are in examples_below_billed with matching MDM and minutes, and C0049846 and C0049854 are low-complexity 99215 claims with matching details. The language is cautious ('a reason to review the records, not a finding'). Next steps are concrete: request charts, have a coder re-score, request the audit trail. The flagged '17' is the 'problems 17%' note-check figure. It comes from the note review outputs and is plausibly legitimate, though it is not on the card. Weaknesses: the headline mixes low-complexity and documentation evidence without tying them together. The 99215 claims cited for low complexity are not shown to have documentation, so the two lines of evidence are not linked. Claims for the top-complexity side are not mentioned. 'No audit trail was received' is a little odd alongside a next step to request the audit trail. The audit-trail request and the 'sampling plan' step are somewhat generic. The 'late 7%' and 'data 7%' figures are unverifiable from the card. Overall it is solid with minor gaps.","problems":["The note-check percentages (problems 17%, late 7%, data 7%) are not on the card, so the 17 figure cannot be verified from the packet.","The low-complexity 99215 examples (C0049846, C0049854) have no documentation shown, so the two evidence lines are not linked.","The audit-trail step contradicts the statement that no audit trail was received, and the sampling-plan step is generic.","Little discussion of the high-complexity 99215 claims or of why some 99215 claims are supported, so the summary is one-sided."]}
